title: CLO 2025.0 - 2D and 3D
description: This video will introduce the functional updates for 2D and 3D. The optimized features will help you edit patterns more precisely and enhance your digital garment design.
transcript:
This video introduces 2D and 3D related functions for everyone.  
In version 2025.0,  
you can set the range of curves and points on the board.  
This means that we can make curve and point edits within the range defined on the board outline line or on internal lines.  
Now let's see how this function operates.  
Change the 2D tool to generate the round and smooth curve tool.  
And switch to a black and white surface.  
On the board, click any straight line, curve, or line.  
Start to edit the range.  
Then click another straight line, curve, or line  
to end the edit range.  
During this operation, a gray reference line will be displayed.  
The reference line can be divided into two parts.  
Stop the mouse wheel on the side to be edited.  
The outline line on this side will turn blue.  
Click it, and it will turn yellow.  
Next, we need to decide which line to edit.  
There are two options.  
One is to click the yellow line on the board outline line or point.  
The other is to click the gray reference line.  
Next, we first click the yellow line on the board outline.  
Then click the yellow line.  
Then click the white line.  
Click and drag the point, straight line, or line.  
Click and drag the line, straight line, or line.  
The selected point or line will be edited and moved.  
The nearby curve and straight line will move proportionally.  
When editing the curve, the number of curve points remains unchanged.  
You can also add other points if needed.  
If you want to edit one point,  
it is possible to press the CTRL key to click and drag the curve or straight line points.  
One point will be edited and moved.  
If you want to edit multiple points,  
first press Shift to select multiple curve points or multiple straight lines.  
If you want to cancel a certain point,  
you can press Shift and then click this point.  
This point will be deselected.  
Then press Ctrl to click and drag them.  
The selected points can be edited and moved.  
Sometimes you may want to move a point by a designated distance.  
At this time, you can press and drag the curve point or straight line.  
During the dragging process, press the right mouse button.  
In the pop-up window, enter the moving distance value.  
So we can edit and move the point according to the designated distance.  
Next, let's explain how to increase the number of points.  
During the dragging process,  
if you want to add more points,  
you can press Ctrl and then click on the line segment.  
You can add a new curve point to the line segment.  
Please note that when adding points to the Bezier curve,  
the curve type will be converted to a sample curve,  
and the curve rate may be adjusted due to this conversion.  
When adding points to the sample curve,  
the curve type remains as a sample curve.  
If you want to delete unnecessary points,  
you can right-click on the selected curve point or straight line point,  
and select Delete from the menu.  
This will delete the selected points.  
If you want to delete multiple points at once,  
you can press Shift to select multiple curve points or multiple straight lines.  
Then right-click on these points,  
and select Delete from the menu.  
This will delete the selected multiple points.  
Next, let's explain how to undo or cancel the editing operation.  
During the editing process,  
we can press Backspace to gradually undo the editing operations.  
If you want to cancel the entire editing process,  
you can press Esc.  
Finally, after adjusting,  
press the Enter key to complete the editing.  
Before pressing the Enter key,  
you can continue to edit the curve until you are satisfied.  
After pressing the Enter key,  
the selection of the outer or inner curve line will be updated according to the latest state after editing.  
If you select the reference line at the beginning,  
note that the straight line points cannot be edited.  
The straight line points will be increased when at the start or end points,  
and will be updated according to the latest state after editing.  
By using this new feature,  
we can select a single version  
and edit the range of definition.  
The other undefined parts will not be affected.  
Therefore, you can only edit the range you need  
to improve the accuracy of the version.  
Next, I will introduce the optimization of labels.  
Now you can proceed to edit the label,  
adjust the direction and color of the label,  
and quickly and clearly access the label information.  
In the 2D window, we have created the label.  
Now we need to name the label.  
First, select the label tool in the toolbar in the 2D window.  
On the label, left-click to enter the name of the label to create it.  
After entering the name on the label, select Edit View Tools.  
Select the label that has just been added.  
In the previous Kolo version,  
when the font size was reduced,  
the view would appear larger.  
But now you can manually adjust the font size  
to prevent the font from becoming too large.  
Go to the property editor and set the font size to 24.  
Now there are several font sizes to choose from.  
It can make the entire version look more beautiful.  
In addition, you can also change the font color.  
Click on the color block next to the color code.  
You can choose the color you like from the color palette.  
For example, red.  
You can also rotate the label.  
Directly stop the mouse at the top of the view.  
After switching to double-click, press and hold.  
Then rotate the label to the desired direction.  
Next, I will introduce how to change the direction of the label according to the angle of the number.  
Select the label and go to the property editor.  
Click on the direction to open the drop-down menu.  
You will find four direction options.  
The default angle 0 means that the label will maintain a horizontal position.  
Angle is 0.  
When you modify the rotation in the 2D window, you will use this option.  
X-axis means that the label will maintain a horizontal position according to the X-axis.  
Y-axis means that the label will maintain a vertical position according to the Y-axis.  
Parallel to the kill line direction means that the label will show the direction of the kill line.  
The update of the label  
allows us to add a personalized label mark.  
It is more convenient to connect to the subsequent production process.  
In the new version, when the label appears in the code,  
the warning window will display the label name with the problem.  
At the same time, it will be displayed in red on the label.  
This makes it convenient for us to quickly locate the problem.  
The label will be corrected in position.  
Open the file containing the label information.  
Open the label in the object window.  
Click on each scale in size.  
Check if each scale can be changed normally.  
During the scale change process,  
if you encounter a scale with wrong label information,  
a warning window will immediately pop up.

as well as the name of the label with the problem.  
This makes it easier for us to find the problematic label and correct it.  
When the warning window pops up,  
the window size will automatically be set to an appropriate size,  
preventing most of the labels from being blocked,  
and showing the wrong location with a prominent red color.

If the distance between the lines is too close, please separate them a little.  
If the distance between the lines is too close, please separate them a little.  
If the distance between the lines is too close, please move or delete the point.  
The outline of the disc is moving.  
The new function greatly improves the efficiency of Fish Value Training.

Scroll down.

Go to the size section and change the unit to percentage.

and apply 5% to the X-axis, the Y-axis will also change proportionally.  
Increasing the X-axis by 5% adds 5% to the original size.  
You can also directly ensure that the sticker scales proportionally in the sticker properties.  
In the object window,  
select the sticker to be applied.  
Under the sticker change information in the property editor,  
you will find the fixed ratio option,  
and select it to use the function.

we can apply the code according to the percentage to complete the proportional scaling of the sticker.  
The latest function for putting codes on stickers makes it easier for you  
to apply codes on stickers proportionally in a faster way.  
If the outer outline of the board or the straight line overlaps with a larger size sticker,  
now we can use the editor to put the code.  
Select the outer outline of the board or the straight line on the line and curve point to put the code on it.

we can see that the board and the larger sticker form an overlap.  
Now we need to select the straight line that overlaps with the sticker.

Select the tool to put the code.  
Click on the straight line.  
A spring appears next to the mouse to allow us to select.

After selecting the name of the board,  
we will select the straight line on the board and then operate to put the code.  
If you want to select the straight line of the inner line of the board to put the code,  
it is the same operation.

use the editor tool to put the code and select the key point of the editor to put the code.  
The property editor will display the corresponding push and pull distance and gap.  
Click on the small arrow on the right side of the icon.  
It will show an independent window for the editor to put the code.  
In this window, the push and pull distance and gap will be displayed on the same level line.  
The values are shown in the list.  
In this window, an illustration appears showing that the position of the table is incorrect.  
Each key point in it is assigned to the position of the table in the raise.  
Here, I will show you how it should be.  
Is it useful for you?  
If you want to appreciate it,  
this is also a new feature of the code release function this time.  
After changing the push and pull distance in this way,  
you can see that the corresponding axis has also changed accordingly, and the window will always remain open when switching to other tools.  
After finishing the edit, click the close button in the upper right corner of the window.  
The window will return to its original state and continue to be displayed in the attribute editor.

You could see that because the virtual model name was too long, it would not display completely.

and the function keys on the right side will all be displayed to switch the horse.

translated the stress map into a hard map,  
and the string map into a hard map.

used to show the pressure of the virtual model from the clothing.

through the grid of the virtual model,  
instead of the version calculating the pressure value,  
provides a more accurate visualization effect,  
and avoids errors in the pressure value and pressure color,  
especially in the case of multi-layer clothing.

we updated the value range of the depth map,  
from the previous maximum of 10,000% to the current 5,000%.

when the human body feels pressure above 5,000%,  
it will feel very tight and unable to wear.

Then simulate the clothing to activate the depth map.

the strength of the depth map is reflected on the surface of the virtual model.

you can display the pressure value of the virtual model in the area,

the color of the part of the virtual model will change.  
If you want to know the pressure value of the part,  
you can stop the simulation and click the Control key to check.  
We hope that the new improvement method can accurately express the pressure area  
and improve the accuracy of version modification,  
thereby optimizing your digital clothing design and try-on process.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - 2D and 3D
chunks.content: # CLO 2025.0 - 2D and 3D Functions Overview This document details the new 2D and 3D functionalities introduced in CLO 2025.0, focusing on curve and point editing ranges, label optimization, proportional sticker scaling, code placement improvements, UI enhancements, model display updates, and the upgraded depth map for pressure visualization in virtual clothing design. --- ## Curve and Point Range Editing on Boards This section explains how to set and edit the range of curves and points on board outlines or internal lines using the new range selection feature in CLO 2025.0. - **Range Setting**: Users can define an editable range on the board by selecting two points (straight line, curve, or line). A gray reference line appears, dividing into editable and non-editable sections. - **Editing Workflow**: 1. Switch to the 2D round and smooth curve tool on a black and white surface. 2. Click on the start and end lines/points to define the edit range; the outline line on the editing side turns blue, then yellow when selected. 3. Choose which line to edit by clicking either the yellow outline line or the gray reference line. 4. Drag points, straight lines, or curves to adjust shapes. Nearby curves and lines move proportionally without changing the total number of curve points. - **Point Editing**: - Hold **Ctrl** and drag to move a single point. - Use **Shift** to select multiple points or lines; deselect points by Shift-clicking again. - Press **Ctrl** and drag to move multiple selected points. - **Moving Points by Specific Distance**: While dragging a point, press the right mouse button to open a pop-up window where a precise movement distance can be entered. - **Adding Points**: Press **Ctrl** and click on a line segment during dragging to add a new curve point. - Adding points converts Bezier curves to sample curves, possibly changing curve behavior. - Adding points to sample curves keeps the curve type unchanged. - **Deleting Points**: Right-click selected points and choose **Delete**. Multiple points can be deleted by selecting with Shift and then deleting. - **Undo and Cancel Editing**: - Press **Backspace** to undo edits step-by-step. - Press **Esc** to cancel all changes. - Press **Enter** to finalize edits, updating the selection of outer or inner curve lines. - **Restrictions**: Editing range defined by the reference line does not allow editing of straight line points directly, except for start/end points which update after editing. - **Use Case**: This feature allows selective editing of defined ranges without affecting undefined areas, improving version accuracy. --- ## Label Optimization in 2D This section covers label creation, naming, customization, and error detection improvements in CLO 2025.0. - **Creating and Naming Labels**: - Select the label tool in the 2D toolbar. - Left-click the label area to enter a name. - **Font Size and Color Control**: - Previous versions enlarged views as font size decreased; now font size is manually adjustable to prevent distortion. - Set font size in the property editor (e.g., size 24).
chunks.content_description: This video will introduce the functional updates for 2D and 3D. The optimized features will help you edit patterns more precisely and enhance your digital garment design.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - 2D and 3D
chunks.content: --- ## Label Optimization in 2D This section covers label creation, naming, customization, and error detection improvements in CLO 2025.0. - **Creating and Naming Labels**: - Select the label tool in the 2D toolbar. - Left-click the label area to enter a name. - **Font Size and Color Control**: - Previous versions enlarged views as font size decreased; now font size is manually adjustable to prevent distortion. - Set font size in the property editor (e.g., size 24). - Change font color via a color palette by clicking the color block next to the color code (e.g., red). - **Label Rotation**: - Rotate labels by double-clicking and holding the mouse on the label top, then dragging to desired orientation. - **Direction Options for Labels**: Accessible via the property editor’s direction dropdown with four options: 1. **Angle 0**: Horizontal position maintained, used for manual rotation. 2. **X-axis**: Label aligns horizontally with the X-axis. 3. **Y-axis**: Label aligns vertically with the Y-axis. 4. **Parallel to Kill Line Direction**: Label aligns with the kill line direction. - **Error Detection and Warning System**: - Labels with issues are highlighted in red both in the code and on the label itself. - Warning windows display the label name and problem description immediately when a scale or label error occurs during size adjustments. - The window resizes automatically to avoid blocking labels and uses prominent red color to mark problematic areas. - **Common Warning Causes**: - Lines too close together requiring separation. - Overlapping or misplaced points affecting outlines. - **Benefit**: These improvements enhance label clarity, facilitate error detection, and streamline production workflow integration. --- ## Proportional Sticker Scaling and Code Application This section explains how to scale stickers proportionally and apply codes precisely using the fixed ratio function. - **Fixed Ratio Scaling**: - In the 2D window, select a sticker and enable **Fixed Ratio** in the property editor to lock width and height scaling proportionally. - Size can be adjusted in percentage units; e.g., entering 5% for X-axis scales both X and Y by 5%. - Useful for resizing decal plates and tags while maintaining aspect ratio. - **Applying Codes on Overlapping Lines and Stickers**: - Users can apply codes on outer or inner board outlines or overlapping straight lines and curve points. - Selecting the line or curve point brings up a spring selector showing board and sticker names for precise code placement. - This supports scenarios where large stickers overlap lines. --- ## Editor UI Enhancements for Code Placement This section details UI improvements that facilitate code editing with push/pull distances and gap displays. - **Independent Window for Distance and Gap**: - When editing code placement, a small arrow next to the push/pull distance and gap icons opens an independent window. - This window lists values on the same level line for easier simultaneous viewing. - **Illustrative Support**: - The window includes a diagram showing correct table positions for reference during editing.
chunks.content_description: This video will introduce the functional updates for 2D and 3D. The optimized features will help you edit patterns more precisely and enhance your digital garment design.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - 2D and 3D
chunks.content: --- ## Editor UI Enhancements for Code Placement This section details UI improvements that facilitate code editing with push/pull distances and gap displays. - **Independent Window for Distance and Gap**: - When editing code placement, a small arrow next to the push/pull distance and gap icons opens an independent window. - This window lists values on the same level line for easier simultaneous viewing. - **Illustrative Support**: - The window includes a diagram showing correct table positions for reference during editing. - **Persistent Window**: - The independent window stays open even when switching tools until manually closed. - Closing returns the display to the property editor view. - **Benefits**: These UI upgrades enable faster, smoother editing of code placement with clear, accessible parameters. --- ## Virtual Model Name Display and Horse Model Switching This section describes improvements in displaying virtual model names and switching between horse models. - **Full Name Display**: - Previous versions truncated long virtual model names under unit machines. - CLO 2025.0 now shows the full virtual model name beneath each horse model. - **Horse Model Switching**: - Users can scroll horizontally or widen the window to view all function keys for switching horses. - This enhances usability when managing multiple models. --- ## Depth Map Update for Pressure Visualization This section explains the upgraded depth map, renamed from stress map and string map, critical for evaluating pressure in virtual clothing. - **Depth Map Function**: Visualizes pressure applied by virtual clothing on the body, aiding in fit and comfort evaluation. - **Improvements in CLO 2025.0**: - Updated translation of the depth map and renamed stress and string maps as hard maps. - Uses a virtual model grid to provide more precise pressure visualization instead of direct pressure calculations, reducing errors, especially with multi-layer garments. - Updated value range reduced maximum from 10,000% to 5,000%, reflecting experimental findings that pressures above 5,000% cause discomfort or inability to wear. - **Usage Instructions**: - Activate depth map by pressing **Shift** in the upper left corner of the 3D window then simulating clothing. - Pressure strength is shown on the virtual model surface; unaffected areas display zero. - To check clothing pressure values: - On Windows, hold **Control** and click the clothing area. - On Mac OS, hold **CMD** and click. - **Dynamic Pressure Feedback**: - Dragging clothing during simulation updates virtual model color to reflect pressure changes. - Stop simulation and use control-click to view exact pressure values. - **Benefits**: This update enhances accuracy in pressure representation, improving design modifications and virtual try-on quality. --- # Summary CLO 2025.0 introduces precise range editing for curves and points, enhanced label customization and error detection, proportional sticker scaling with fixed ratio, improved code placement UI, better virtual model name management, and a significantly refined depth map for pressure visualization. These features collectively improve accuracy, efficiency, and usability in digital clothing design and virtual fitting workflows.
